definitions.meaning: first meaning: settled or resolved, as in a past-tense verb
second meaning: firmly focused on one goal

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to commit wholeheartedly to one aim.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of a verb meaning settled on and an adjective meaning resolute or unwavering.

clue.text: Dull shade of carpet used in the computer room

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

parts.note: mouse is a dull greyish-brown colour, as in mousy hair
a mat is a small piece of floor covering

explanation.surface: A drab-coloured rug laid on the floor of an office full of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: The small pad a pointing device glides over sits on desks wherever computers are worked on.

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing set on another sits above it, so the second word comes first

parts.note: taken as written
to rely is to depend

explanation.surface: A reassuring plea: you can count on me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an opener meaning simply, and it is the definition in that very sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely and just are adverb synonyms, both meaning only or no more than.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to flatter or fuss over someone obsequiously
second meaning: a young deer in its first year

explanation.surface: A doting adult lavishes affection on a child.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to show servile affection; as a noun it names a baby deer.

clue.text: They're not positive when foreign spies meet fog

indicators.note: the two parts meet end to end, so one simply follows the other
foreign suggests something alien and unfamiliar, so the letters of spies appear in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
as a verb, to fog is to cloud over, and it mists over in the same sense

explanation.surface: Foreign agents lost in a fog are unlikely to feel confident.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged spies come first and the clouding-over verb follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pessimists expect the worst, so they are the opposite of positive-thinking people.

parts.note: surface reading: a team entering a competition or tournament
setter's reading: a team is a side, and an entry is a door, so a door for a side

explanation.walkthrough: Team reads as a sporting word, but a team is also called a side, and that side names a way in at the flank of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary entrance at the flank of a building, rather than the front, is how one gets in.

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife harbours a grudge against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spite or the intention to do harm, a direct synonym of ill-will.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to perceive by touch or intuition
second meaning: the mood or character of a place

explanation.surface: Someone picks up on the mood in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means perceive; as a noun it is the general impression a place gives.

clue.text: Declare innocent of sole charge laid against former partner

indicators.note: placing one thing up against another sets them side by side, end to end

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
sole means single, only one
a rate is a price or fee charged

explanation.surface: A court clears someone of the one charge an ex-spouse brought against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks legal, matching the courtroom picture, but it is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame, officially declaring them not guilty.

clue.text: In a fury, I tear around

indicators.note: tearing around is careering about wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry person storms about the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, an adjective matching the phrase describing someone furious.

clue.text: Form of art seen is of oriental origin

indicators.note: a new form of something is a reshaping, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A style of art on display comes from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is an older word for Asian, and eastern describes things coming from that part of the world.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: out of the ordinary, exceptional
second meaning: a dish offered that day beyond the usual menu

explanation.surface: A diner praises a remarkable meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning exceptional and a noun for a chef's dish of the day.

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: something well preserved
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an embalmed body, as in ancient Egypt
second meaning: a mother, in British spelling

explanation.surface: A relative who looks good for their age.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a flattering remark about an older relative; the joke is that an embalmed body is very well preserved indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian embalmed corpses survive millennia, and the same word is the British spelling of a child's name for its mother.

clue.text: Bit of a heartless remark about horse failing to finish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remark goes around the horse
without a heart, the word loses the letter at its centre

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: not reaching the end means the horse's final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A cruel remark about a racehorse that did not complete the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to finish' sounds like the horse's race, but it trims the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is a part or element of a larger whole, so a bit of something.

parts.note: surface reading: a shop selling locks, alarms and safes
setter's reading: links used to secure things, and a shop for them, which in fact names one of many branches under a single owner

explanation.walkthrough: The question suggests a specialist security shop; read literally it is a store for links of metal, which is also the name for a retailer with many branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer with many identical branches under one owner is named by joining the word for linked metal and a shop.

clue.text: Overstepped permit to enter wilderness on return

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the permit sits within the other word
returning means going back the way one came, so the wilderness is read backwards

parts.note: a desert is a barren wilderness
a pass is a permit allowing entry

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a permit to go into the desert on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go beyond a boundary without right, and overstepped is its past tense synonym.

clue.text: It once swelled the ranks at country church event

parts.note: national means belonging to a country
a service is an act of worship in church

explanation.surface: A national religious gathering drew bigger crowds than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: This was Britain's peacetime conscription, which ended in 1960; it filled the armed forces' ranks with young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory military duty for young British men, abolished around 1960, enlarged the army with conscripts.

clue.text: Pain and toil involved in creating works of art

definitions.note: a phrase describing the material's use, not a noun

indicators.note: involved means tangled and intricate, so the letters are twisted together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making art takes suffering and hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment mixed with linseed is a classic medium used by painters to produce canvases.

clue.text: It's annoying when I r-rant about it

definitions.note: a clause describing the noun: something annoying

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rant goes around the final word

parts.note: taken as written
the stammered first letter of the next word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stammers in fury while ranting about something irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is no typo: the extra letter is part of the answer, and the final pronoun sits inside the rant.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that causes annoyance or physical irritation.

parts.note: surface reading: restrictions on what an author may write
setter's reading: the time limits by which copy must be handed in

explanation.walkthrough: Limits suggests censorship or word counts, but the limits meant are dates and times that journalists and authors must deliver by.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists and authors face fixed times for submitting copy, which bound how long they may work.

indicators.note: something expressed in words is carried within them, so the answer lies inside the phrase

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rallying song voices a one-sided political message.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, often of a nation or cause.

indicators.note: turning something up flips it over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: parts as a verb means divides or splits

explanation.surface: A music group breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splits up band' reads as a group disbanding; 'band' is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a narrow strip of leather or fabric, which is one meaning of band.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a place where water rises from the ground

explanation.surface: A water source that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective meaning no charge, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring a prisoner is informal for helping them escape; a spring is also natural groundwater welling up.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone takes back what they said about a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or disavow something said earlier.

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Choosing the proper moment to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is violent fury, a noun synonym for strong displeasure.

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk swears at the priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Curates are assistant priests in a parish, so they are members of the clergy.

parts.note: Cos is the abbreviation for companies
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Companies are badly affected by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit hard' reads as one phrase about an economic blow, but it splits into the definition and a single letter. A cosh is a British word for a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them on the head with a club or bludgeon.

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a fresh perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather or pick up bit by bit, originally collecting leftover grain.

clue.text: Tinker with on-screen, adding a sound effect

indicators.note: to tinker with something is to fiddle with it and reorganise its parts

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, joined to the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A film editor adjusts what is on screen and adds an audio effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is the deep, prolonged quality of a reverberating tone, an acoustic phenomenon.
